summary: The candidate is a credible partial implementation for eager, fixed-width DeepSeek NextN draft-extend with segmented A2A. Its focused unit suite passes and independent single-GPU tensor checks confirm its split/recombine mechanics. The original issue's decisive behavior was not verified: the candidate's own coverage proof requires a 4-GPU DeepEP deployment and DeepSeek target/NextN weights, while this review had one GPU and no qualifying weights. CUDA-graph draft-extend, widened/multi-layer draft inputs, non-segmented dispatch, context parallelism, and other draft architectures remain unsupported or gated off, so this is not a complete implementation of the open feature request.

gpu_execution_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) executed independent tensor-level numerical checks. No model forward or multi-GPU DeepEP execution was possible.
remaining_counterexamples: With draft-extend CUDA graph replay enabled (the normal path unless SGLANG_DISABLE_DRAFT_EXTEND_CUDA_GRAPH=1), the candidate gate disables draft-extend TBO.
EagleDraftExtendInput with num_front_tokens > 0 (widened/multi-layer input) is rejected by an assertion rather than supported.
A none/non-segmented speculative MoE A2A backend leaves draft-extend TBO disabled.
Attention context parallelism greater than one leaves draft-extend TBO disabled.
Draft architectures other than DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN leave draft-extend TBO disabled.

No executed evidence shows that a real 4-GPU DeepEP draft-extend batch enters both TBO children without collective mismatch, preserves GSM8K accuracy and speculative acceptance length, or doubles the running-batch limit described by the issue.
remaining_limitations: The review environment exposed one AMD Instinct MI350X GPU; the candidate integration test is registered for four H100-class GPUs.
The required DeepSeek-V3 target and NextN draft model weights were unavailable. The tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify this architecture, segmented A2A, or distributed behavior.
All candidate changes are Python; repository-environment.json reports native=null. No native rebuild was applicable, and imports were confirmed from /job/repo/python rather than an installed package.
The candidate's functional integration and claimed capacity improvement therefore remain unverified even though its isolated mechanics are well tested.
